## Context
Operator-approved (2026-08-12): make ticket-directory creation atomic so interrupted-write debris cannot occur. Evidence: fsck found 8 empty stray ticket dirs (MISSING_CREATE + FOREIGN_STORE_PATH), all the `makedirs`-then-die signature — the dir existed before its CREATE event file did, and an interruption (host sleep, kill, timeout) in that window strands a plausible-looking empty ticket dir in the tracker worktree. Swept manually under illsuited-erect-ibis (7c6e-4b8a-59c5-46db); bug 043f ("tolerate, never tidy") rejects automatic cleanup of STORE DATA, so prevention at the writer is the self-healing fix.

## Mechanism (confirmed against origin/main abf3817187)
`_store/event_append.py::_prepare_event` — shared by the single-event `stage_and_commit` and by `batch_stage_and_commit`, so BOTH inherit this window — runs `os.makedirs(ticket_dir, exist_ok=True)` at line 171, OUTSIDE the write lock; the first event file only lands at the `os.replace` in `stage_and_commit` (line 425), after the temp write, `write_lock` acquisition and the rebase guard. Death in that window leaves an empty ticket dir, which fsck flags TWICE: `fsck.py::_scan` Check 2 emits MISSING_CREATE (reduce yields None) and `fsck.py::foreign_store_path_list` emits FOREIGN_STORE_PATH (no event file). Both scanners already skip dot-prefixed top-level entries — the convention this fix relies on.

## Design
New leaf module `src/rebar/_store/staging.py` owning the convention and the atomic publish:
- Convention: staging dirs are `<tracker>/.tmp-newticket-<pid>-<uuid4hex>`. The leading dot is the EXISTING exclusion rule already honoured by `fsck._ticket_dirs`, `fsck.foreign_store_path_list`, fsck Check 1 and `relation_snapshot`, so temp paths are invisible to both checks with no scanner change. Documented in the module docstring and docs/concurrency.md.
- `stage_event(...)` -> `StagedEvent`: when the ticket dir does NOT exist, mkdir the staging dir and write the canonical event bytes INSIDE it; when it already exists, keep today's `.tmp-event-*` file staging unchanged.
- BOTH consumers of `_prepare_event` are converted, not just the single-event one. `_prepare_event` is called at `event_append.py:415` (`stage_and_commit`) AND at `:519` (`batch_stage_and_commit`, driven by `_io/import_ndjson.py` and the reconciler flush in `_commands/_seam.py`), so the fix is made in the shared function and both call sites promote through `StagedEvent` — the batch loop replaces its per-event `os.replace` with `promote()` inside the SINGLE existing batch lock, and `_rollback_batch` discards staged trees and rmdirs any ticket dir that batch itself created. The batch path carries the identical makedirs-then-die signature today (its docstring already concedes 'a crash mid-batch ... leaves at most orphaned worktree files'), and fixing the shared function is what closes it for both.
- `StagedEvent.promote()` runs UNDER the existing write lock (lock discipline unchanged): re-checks the final path and either `os.rename(staging_dir, ticket_dir)` — one atomic step publishing dir+CREATE together — or, if a concurrent create won the race, `os.replace(staging_file, final_path)` + rmdir. Staying under the lock keeps an event file invisible until `under_lock_check` (optimistic concurrency) has passed.
- Failure/rollback paths remove the staging tree; a transaction that created the ticket dir then rolled back also rmdirs the now-empty dir it just created, under the lock, in the same transaction.
- `sweep_stale_staging(tracker)`: bounded, best-effort, at ticket-create writer start. Removes ONLY `.tmp-newticket-*` dirs whose owner is provably gone, reusing `lock_owner`'s v2 stamp (host + pid-namespace + start time), which already defeats pid recycling; an absent or unprobeable stamp falls back to a conservative age guard. Bounded scan/removal caps.

043f boundary: the sweep touches ONLY the writer's own staging area (`.tmp-newticket-*`), never a ticket directory and never store data. It does not reintroduce writer-side cleanup of event-less ticket dirs, which stays rejected; the code comment says so.

## AC4 audit — other dir-then-first-file sites in the store write path
Convert (same signature, same tracker, fsck-visible): `_store/event_append.py::batch_stage_and_commit` (shares `_prepare_event`, so it is covered by the same change rather than separately — called from `_io/import_ndjson.py` and the `_commands/_seam.py` reconciler flush); `_engine/rebar_reconciler/inbound_translate.py::_write_event_file` (mkdir precedes `_seam.finalize_event`, which can raise CommandError on the secret screen, and lock acquisition, which can time out) and `_engine/rebar_reconciler/dispatch_one.py` BRIDGE_ALERT emission (mkdir then first alert file).
Exempt with reasons: `_store/lock.py::_acquire_mkdir` (dot-prefixed `.ticket-write.lock.d`, invisible to fsck; its mkdir->stamp gap already has a staleness adjudicator); `_store/hlc.py` and `_commands/fsck_repair.py` marker dirs (under `.rebar/` or the resolved git dir, outside the committed worktree); `session_log.py`, `identity.py`, `trusted_env_cmd.py` pointer/config writers (not in the tracker).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] AC1 — Ticket creation stages dir+CREATE atomically: killing the writer at any point between staging start and rename leaves NO path that fsck reports as MISSING_CREATE/FOREIGN_STORE_PATH (temp paths are excluded from both checks by naming convention, documented).
- [x] AC2 — A RED test simulates the interruption (kill/exception injected between mkdir and event write in the OLD code shape) proving the debris signature, and the fix turns it green; a rename-crash test proves the temp path is invisible to fsck and cleaned on the next writer's start (bounded, best-effort temp sweep of stale temp paths owned by dead pids — this does not violate 043f since temp paths are the writer's own staging area, not store data).
- [x] AC3 — Concurrency: two concurrent creates of different tickets don't collide on temp paths (pid/uuid-suffixed staging names); the existing write-lock discipline is unchanged.
- [x] AC4 — Any other same-signature dir-then-file sites in the store write path are converted or explicitly recorded as exempt with reasons.
- [x] AC5 — make lint/typecheck pass; store suite green; no change to event formats or committed layout.

## Testing
New `tests/interfaces/store/` test module:
1. RED-shape reproduction: inject an exception where the OLD shape wrote the first event (staging fails after the dir would have been made) and assert `fsck.foreign_store_path_list` plus the MISSING_CREATE scan report the ticket id — the debris signature; the converted writer leaves zero findings under the same injection.
2. Crash-before-rename: fail `os.replace`/the lock; assert a `.tmp-newticket-*` path exists and that both `foreign_store_path_list` and the MISSING_CREATE scan return nothing for it (invisibility by convention).
3. Sweep: plant one staging dir stamped with a dead owner and one stamped live; run a create; assert the dead one is gone, the live one untouched, and no ticket directory touched.
4. Concurrency (AC3): two creates of different tickets in flight produce distinct staging names and both land.
5. AC4 converted sites have their own coverage: a test drives `inbound_translate._write_event_file` with `_seam.finalize_event` patched to raise (the secret-screen refusal path) and asserts no fsck-visible directory is left behind; a test drives the `dispatch_one` BRIDGE_ALERT emission with the alert write failing and asserts the same. A batch test drives `batch_stage_and_commit` with a mid-batch failure across two NEW ticket ids and asserts zero MISSING_CREATE/FOREIGN_STORE_PATH findings afterwards.
6. Byte parity unchanged: existing `test_canonical_event_bytes.py` / `test_store.py` residue assertions stay green.
Commands: `make lint`, `make typecheck`, `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_store.py tests/unit/test_store_batch_write.py tests/interfaces/store`.
